decisionSource: The issuer's own current publication: the Vermont Judiciary statewide forms library row for 200-00130, the Judiciary's Expunging and Sealing Criminal Records self-help page and the media node that page links, and the form binary that node serves; read against the integrated Vermont legal-design memo, the regenerated track-source audit, the authoritative blocker ledger, the official-PDF production queue and source-assignment projection, the repository asset audit, the adopted Master Library Edition 1.2 archive entry and state manifest, 13 V.S.A. § 7602 as amended by 2025 Act 60 read at legislature.vermont.gov, and the official Vermont Judiciary captures in the Internet Archive CDX index used only to date supersession.
whatThisDocumentIs: The decision record that settles the source identity of Vermont form 200-00130. The projection carried the identity key rcap-vt-200-00130-b0ad96be1d as unresolved_identity with a placeholder role of PETITION, no bytes, no page count, no issuer and no structural class. This record establishes the document behind the number from the issuer's own publication rather than from the manifest row, the memo, a filename or a neighbouring form number: its existence, exact title, issuer, revision, role, signatory, scope, authority level, official landing page and binary URL, exact measured bytes and PDF structure, the six tracks and six components that consume it, the supersession of an older revision of the same number that is still reachable at a legacy static path, whether an authority-edition amendment is required, and the single mechanical residual that remains. It does not amend the integrated Vermont memo, does not create a source receipt, does not materialize or commit a binary, does not regenerate a registry, queue or projection, does not implement a renderer, does not publish or amend an authority edition, and does not assert that any Vermont implementation family is ready.

scopeOfThisJob.note: The assignment's stop condition reserves memo amendment, source receipts, registry and projection regeneration, edition publication and implementation to other owners. Everything this record establishes is stated here and applied elsewhere by Session A at integration.

questionPresented.conflictAsReported: Three things were open. First, the Judiciary's own materials name the document inconsistently: the narrative Steps prose on the expungement page still calls 200-00130 the 'Petition to Expunge or Seal Criminal History', while the same page's Forms list and the forms-library row call it 'Petition to Seal Criminal History'. The integrated memo resolved that against the PDFs and recorded the narrative as the stale artefact; this job confirms or refutes that at source. Second, the adopted edition asserts an asset at REV-2025-07 with SHA-256 ff914f49c2a78a8b96d48f1242b70ab12ff7cb25beeeb8b850505357fdf982ed and there is no private-corpus candidate for it, so the manifest row had to be confirmed against the issuer rather than adopted. Third, Vermont is known to serve two live binaries per form number, so the current object had to be taken from the issuer's own pointer rather than constructed from the form number.

role.roleBasis: The opening recital reads 'The above-named Defendant hereby requests that the Court order that his/her criminal history record be sealed. As grounds for the request, Defendant hereby states as follows'. A full text extraction of both pages returns exactly one signature block, 'Signature of Defendant', with 'Printed Name of Defendant', address, city/state/zip, phone and email beneath it, and a 'Date of Signature' line. There is no order recital, no decretal language, no findings block, no judge or clerk signature line, no grant or deny disposition, and no prosecutor signature block. The only outside-party artefact is the service line 'cc: State's Attorney or Attorney General's Office', which is a copy instruction, not a signature obligation. It is therefore a participant submission and must not be mapped into an order slot, a stipulation slot, an instructions slot or an outside-party slot.

authorityLevel.petitionAuthority: 13 V.S.A. § 7602(a)(2): 'A person may file a petition with the court requesting sealing of a criminal history record related to a conviction if the person was convicted of a qualifying crime or qualifying crimes arising out of the same incident or occurrence.' Section 7602 was amended by 2025 Act 60, § 1, effective 2025-07-01. The no-conviction sealing route is 13 V.S.A. § 7603 and the 18-to-21 route is 13 V.S.A. § 7609.
authorityLevel.statuteNamesNoForm: Section 7602 confers the right to file a petition and prescribes no form, no form number and no format. Nothing in the section, or in § 7603 or § 7609 as summarized by the issuer's own page, requires this document.
authorityLevel.issuerDirection: The Judiciary's expungement page directs the participant to 'Fill out the Petition to Expunge or Seal Criminal History form (200-00130)' in its narrative Steps, and lists 'Petition to Seal Criminal History (200-00130)' under the heading 'Asking to Seal Records' in its Forms section.
authorityLevel.issuerFormsCaveat: The Judiciary's About Court Forms page states 'There isn't a court form for every situation' and contemplates generic forms adapted by the participant or drafted by an attorney, so no Vermont form may be asserted as mandatory purely because the Judiciary publishes it.
authorityLevel.conclusion: The right to petition is conferred by statute, not by this form; the statute prescribes no form number. 200-00130 is the issuer's single published statewide instrument for exercising the sealing right in the Criminal Division and is controlling as such. It is not established as mandatory by rule or administrative order, and this record does not assert that it is. Its use in the Vermont packets stays required in the petition role exactly as the adopted design has it, because a sealing track has no relief without a petition, not because the form number is compelled.
authorityLevel.coverageOfMultipleSealingRoutes: One form serves every sealing route. Question 2 of the current revision branches between 'I was convicted of the offenses' and 'I was not convicted for the offenses listed above', and the second branch offers the three no-conviction fact patterns — cited or arrested but never charged, charged but no probable cause found, charged and later dismissed — which are the § 7603 routes. The Judiciary publishes no separate no-conviction, 18-to-21 or post-pardon sealing petition. The one-to-many binding across six sealing tracks is therefore a property of the issuer's own form design, not an assumption made by the mapping.

supersessionTreatment.trap: The legacy static path still returns HTTP 200 and a well-formed 46-field AcroForm carrying the same form number, so a binding built against it downloads cleanly and looks right. It is not merely an older revision with a different field set. Its printed title is 'PETITION TO EXPUNGE OR SEAL CRIMINAL HISTORY' and its question 4 asks the participant to elect 'Expunged (all records destroyed except certificate of expungement)' or 'Sealed (records maintained but under seal meaning they are not public)'. Act 60 split that single instrument into two, 200-00129 for expungement and 200-00130 for sealing, and the current revision has no election. Binding the 2018 object into any of the six sealing components would put an expungement election, and a remedy the track does not offer, in front of a sealing participant, and the failure would be silent. Retained availability is not currency, and a legacy URL returning HTTP 200 does not establish currentness.
supersessionTreatment.supersessionEvidence: Both objects carry the same printed form number 200-00130 and the same issuer, so the 07/2025 object is a revision of the same document rather than a different form. The issuer's current self-help page and current forms-library row both point at the 07/2025 object and neither links the legacy path. The archive shows the combined title live on 2025-05-23 and the sealing-only title live on 2025-07-09, bracketing the Act 60 effective date of 2025-07-01, and the current object's own PDF creation timestamp is 2025-07-01.

requiredQuestions.a: Yes. It is a current Vermont Judiciary statewide form. The Judiciary forms library returns exactly one row for the number, filtered to Court Division: Criminal and Language: English, and the Judiciary's own Expunging and Sealing Criminal Records page lists it under 'Asking to Seal Records'. The binary is publicly retrievable.

requiredQuestions.q: What is its exact official title?
requiredQuestions.a: Petition to Seal Criminal History. The printed heading is 'PETITION TO SEAL CRIMINAL HISTORY' and the printed footer on both pages reads '200-00130 – Petition to Seal Criminal History (07/2025)'. The forms-library row and the self-help page Forms list both use the same title. The Judiciary's narrative prose still uses the pre-Act 60 title 'Petition to Expunge or Seal Criminal History'; that layer is stale.
The Vermont Judiciary, for the Criminal Division of the Vermont Superior Court. Not a local court, not a prosecutor, not a commercial publisher.

requiredQuestions.q: Is it a petition, application, motion, affidavit, stipulation, notice, order, instructions, fee-waiver component or outside-party instrument?
requiredQuestions.a: A petition. It carries a single signature block, 'Signature of Defendant', an opening recital in the words of the defendant requesting an order, and no decretal language, findings block, judge or clerk signature line, or prosecutor signature block. It is not an application, motion, affidavit, stipulation, notice, order, instruction sheet, fee-waiver component or outside-party instrument.

Yes. It is completed and filed by the person seeking relief, published on a public self-help page addressed to the petitioner, and served as a fillable PDF the Judiciary tells the public to type into and file.

The defendant, that is the petitioner, and no one else. There is exactly one signature block. The prosecutor does not sign this form; the prosecutor signs 200-00132, the stipulation. The court does not sign it. The petitioner's signature and date remain a manual completion item.

Yes. It is published in the statewide forms library rather than by a unit, and its own Unit dropdown enumerates all fourteen Vermont counties. Vermont has a unified Superior Court and one statewide form set, and no county variant of this form exists. It is Criminal Division only and English only.

requiredQuestions.q: Is it mandatory, controlling, optional, or merely a reference?
requiredQuestions.a: Controlling as the Judiciary's single published statewide instrument for a sealing petition, and required in the petition role because a sealing track has no relief without a petition. It is not mandatory by rule or number: 13 V.S.A. § 7602(a)(2) confers the right to 'file a petition with the court' and prescribes no form, and the Judiciary's About Court Forms page states there is not a form for every situation and contemplates adapted or drafted documents. This record does not assert the form is mandatory.
Six: vt_seal_18_to_21, vt_seal_dui, vt_seal_felony, vt_seal_misdemeanor, vt_seal_nonconviction and vt_seal_pardon. Not vt_exp_decriminalized, which uses 200-00129.

Six, each in the petition role: vt_seal_18_to_21-petition-1, vt_seal_dui-petition-1, vt_seal_felony-petition-1, vt_seal_misdemeanor-petition-1, vt_seal_nonconviction-petition-2 and vt_seal_pardon-petition-1.

requiredQuestions.q: Has it been superseded, renumbered, merged, or retired?
requiredQuestions.a: None of those at the document level. The number, the issuer and the role class are unchanged and the form is current. What changed at the 07/2025 revision is the title and the scope: the pre-Act 60 revision was a combined expunge-or-seal petition with an election, and Act 60 split it so that 200-00130 seals and 200-00129 expunges. requiredQuestions.q: Does resolving it unlock one or more Vermont implementation families?
requiredQuestions.a: No, and this record does not claim it does. It removes the unresolved_identity blocker from rcap-vt-flat-pdf-overlay and rcap-vt-composed-route on the merits, but both remain blocked by identity_resolved_materialization_required for 600-00228, the composed route additionally depends on the overlay job, and 200-00130 itself carries the materialization blocker until a receipt exists. rcap-vt-acroform-fill is unaffected.

requiredQuestions.q: Is an authority-edition amendment required before materialization?
requiredQuestions.a: No. This is the point on which 200-00130 differs from 600-00228. The adopted Edition 1.2 already retains the exact bytes at the canonical archive path STATES/VT/02_PACKET_FORMS/VT__FORM__200-00130__petition-to-seal-criminal-history__REV-2025-07__EN.pdf and already manifests the row correctly: assetClass packet_form, packetCandidate true, revision REV-2025-07, SHA-256 ff914f49c2a78a8b96d48f1242b70ab12ff7cb25beeeb8b850505357fdf982ed, and in the state manifest a byte count of 1,535,506, technicalClass acroform_pdf and pageCount 2, with the correct official URL. There is nothing to reclassify and nothing to measure. 200-00130 does not appear in authority-edition-amendment-handoff.json and does not belong there. Materialization can proceed through the ordinary portable path.

It is not merely an older field set: it carries an expunge-or-seal election that Act 60 removed, so binding it into a sealing component would offer a remedy the track does not provide, and the failure would be silent rather than a retrieval error.

evidenceLimits: No source binary is committed, materialized or added to any sealed root by this record. The form is recorded by official URL and by exact measured identity only. The binary was retrieved to a scratch location outside the worktree, measured, and left there.

Currency is established from the issuer's own pointers — the Expunging and Sealing Criminal Records self-help page link and the forms-library row — and from the printed footer of the served binary. It is not established from the filename, the folder, a neighbouring form number, the private corpus, a search-engine result or the fact that a URL returns HTTP 200.

legislature.vermont.gov presents an incomplete TLS chain from this environment, omitting the GlobalSign RSA OV SSL CA 2018 intermediate. The statutory text of 13 V.S.A. § 7602 was retrieved after supplying that intermediate from the certificate's own CA Issuers URI. This is an access condition, not a currency or authenticity finding; the served certificate is validly issued to State of Vermont, Montpelier, and is current at the retrieval date.

web.archive.org was queried only through its CDX index, and only to date the supersession and to test whether the legacy path was ever archived. Its returns were controlled against a form number known to exist at that path shape. The archive is never used here as authority for what the current form is.

Whether any Vermont Rule of Criminal Procedure or Supreme Court administrative order makes this form mandatory was not established, and no mandatory status is asserted. The Judiciary hosts its rules off-site through a commercial publisher, which is not usable as controlling evidence, and its own About Court Forms page declines to treat its form set as exhaustive.

No unofficial mirror, commercial form site, Justia, FindLaw or search-engine snippet was used or consulted as controlling evidence, and no conclusion in this record rests on filename similarity or on a private-corpus row.
